<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">PART&nbsp;I</font></b><a name="Parti_161215"></a></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Item 1.&#160; Business.</font></b><a name="Item1_Business__161218"></a></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">INTRODUCTION</font></b></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Courier Corporation, together with its subsidiaries, (&#147;Courier,&#148; the &#147;Company,&#148; &#147;We,&#148; &#147;Our,&#148; or &#147;Us&#148;) is among America&#146;s largest book manufacturers and a leader in content management and customization in new and traditional media.&#160; The Company also publishes books under three brands offering award-winning content and thousands of titles. Courier Corporation, founded in 1824, was incorporated under the laws of Massachusetts on June&nbsp;30, 1972.&#160; The Company has two operating segments: book manufacturing and publishing.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The book manufacturing segment focuses on streamlining the process of bringing books from the point of creation to the point of use.&#160; Based on sales, Courier is the third largest book manufacturer in the United States, offering services from prepress and production through storage and distribution, as well as innovative content management, customization, and state-of-the-art digital print capabilities. Courier&#146;s principal book manufacturing markets are religious, education and specialty trade. Revenues from this segment accounted for approximately 90% of Courier&#146;s consolidated sales in fiscal 2013.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The publishing segment consists of Dover Publications,&nbsp;Inc. (&#147;Dover&#148;), Research&nbsp;&amp; Education Association,&nbsp;Inc. (&#147;REA&#148;), and Federal Marketing Corporation, d/b/a Creative Homeowner (&#147;Creative Homeowner&#148;).&#160; Dover publishes over 10,000 titles in more than 30 specialty categories including children&#146;s books, literature, art, music, crafts, mathematics, science, religion and architecture.&#160; REA publishes test preparation and study guide books for high school, college and graduate students, and professionals.&#160; Creative Homeowner publishes books on home design, decorating, landscaping and gardening, and also sells home plans. Revenues in this segment were approximately 14% of consolidated sales in fiscal 2013.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The combination of Dover&#146;s, REA&#146;s, and Creative Homeowner&#146;s publishing, sales and distribution skills with Courier&#146;s book manufacturing, digital content conversion, and e-commerce skills provides a comprehensive end-to-end solution for Courier&#146;s customers.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Additional segment information, including the amounts of operating income and total assets, for each of the last three fiscal years, is contained in Note M in the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements included in this Annual Report on Form&nbsp;10-K.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">OPERATING SEGMENTS</font></b></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">BOOK MANUFACTURING SEGMENT</font></b></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Courier&#146;s book manufacturing segment produces hard and softcover books, manages content and provides warehousing and distribution services for its customers, which include publishers, religious organizations and other information providers.&#160; Courier provides book manufacturing and related services from five facilities in Westford and North Chelmsford, Massachusetts; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania; and Kendallville and Terre Haute,&nbsp;Indiana.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On April&nbsp;30, 2013, the Company acquired all of the outstanding stock of FastPencil,&nbsp;Inc. (&#147;FastPencil&#148;), a California-based developer of end-to-end, cloud-based content management technologies. FastPencil&#146;s technology serves publishers and other companies interested in providing a self-publishing platform to their customers or communities. In addition, FastPencil provides a platform</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">1<a name="PB_1_161813_7056"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">and services to thousands of self-publishers. The acquisition complements the Company&#146;s content management and customization technology and gives the Company an entry into the rapidly growing self-publishing market. The Company paid $5 million at the time of acquisition, with additional future &#147;earn out&#148; potential payments, conditioned upon the achievement of revenue targets with a maximum payout of three payments of up to $6.5 million, $1.25 million and $5.25 million which may be paid out over the next five years. The acquisition was accounted for as a purchase and, accordingly, FastPencil&#146;s financial results are included in the book manufacturing segment in the consolidated financial statements from the date of acquisition.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On January&nbsp;15, 2010, the Company acquired the assets of Highcrest Media LLC (&#147;Highcrest Media&#148;), a Massachusetts-based provider of solutions that streamline the production of customized textbooks and other materials for use in colleges, universities and businesses.&#160; The acquisition of Highcrest Media complements the Company&#146;s investments during fiscal years 2010 and 2011 in digital printing technology. The $3 million cash acquisition was accounted for as a purchase, and accordingly, Highcrest Media&#146;s financial results are included in the book manufacturing segment in the consolidated financial statements from the date of acquisition.&#160; Additional &#147;earn out&#148; payments of $1.2 million were earned and paid by the Company in the three years following the acquisition of Highcrest Media.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In the second quarter of fiscal 2011, the Company closed its Stoughton, Massachusetts manufacturing facility due to the impact of technology and competitive pressures affecting the one-color paperback books in which the plant specialized.&#160; The Company consolidated the Stoughton operations into its other manufacturing facilities.&#160; In fiscal 2012, the Company further reduced its one-color offset press capacity at its Westford, Massachusetts facility.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Courier&#146;s book manufacturing operations utilize both offset and digital print technologies, combined with various binding capabilities, to produce both soft and hard cover books.&#160; Each of Courier&#146;s five facilities work together, although each has certain specialties adapted to the needs of the market niches Courier serves, such as printing on lightweight paper, book cover production, four-color book manufacturing, and digital printing.&#160; These services are primarily sold to publishers of educational, religious and trade books.&#160; The Company has four-color offset book manufacturing capabilities with four manroland offset presses at its Kendallville,&nbsp;Indiana facility.&#160; During 2010, the Company built a state-of-the-art digital printing operation at its North Chelmsford, Massachusetts facility through a relationship with HP and installed two more digital presses in fiscal 2011. In fiscal 2013, a complete digital production line was installed at the Kendallville,&nbsp;Indiana facility and the Company announced plans to install a second digital press in Kendallville in fiscal 2014.&#160; These digital print capabilities, combined with Highcrest Media and FastPencil, comprise the Company&#146;s newest market offerings, Courier New Media and Courier Digital Solutions. In addition, Highcrest Media manages content for leading financial services companies.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has Chain-of-Custody certifications by two leading environmental organizations, the Sustainable Forestry Initiative (SFI) and the Programme for the Endorsement of Forestry Certification (PEFC). This new dual certification complements Courier&#146;s existing certification by the Forest Stewardship Council (FSC) and marks the Company as &#147;triple-certified&#148; for its systematic adherence to environmentally responsible practices in the use of paper and other forest products throughout its manufacturing locations.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Courier&#146;s book manufacturing sales force of 15 people is responsible for all of the Company&#146;s sales to almost 400 book-manufacturing customers.&#160; Courier&#146;s salespeople operate out of sales offices located in New York, New York; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania; Terre Haute,&nbsp;Indiana; Campbell, California; and North Chelmsford, Massachusetts.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Sales to Pearson Education,&nbsp;Inc. aggregated approximately 33% of consolidated sales in fiscal 2013 and 30% of consolidated sales in both fiscal years 2012 and 2011. Sales to The Gideons International aggregated approximately 23% of consolidated sales in fiscal 2013, 25% in fiscal 2012 and 23% in fiscal 2011.&#160; A significant reduction in order volumes or price levels from these customers could have a material adverse effect on the Company.&#160; No other customer accounted for more than 10% of consolidated sales in any of the past three fiscal years.&#160; The Company distributes products around the</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">world; export sales, as a percentage of consolidated sales, were approximately 23% in fiscal 2013, 21% in fiscal 2012 and 20% in fiscal 2011.&#160; Approximately 95% of the export sales were in the book manufacturing segment in fiscal year 2013, 92% in fiscal 2012 and 90% in fiscal year 2011.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">All phases of Courier&#146;s business are highly competitive.&#160; The printing industry has almost 48,000 establishments.&#160; While most of these companies are relatively small, several of the Company&#146;s competitors are considerably larger or are affiliated with companies that are considerably larger and have greater financial resources than Courier.&#160; In recent years, consolidation of both customers and competitors within the Company&#146;s markets has increased pricing pressures.&#160; The major competitive factors in Courier&#146;s book manufacturing business in addition to price are product quality, speed of delivery, customer service, availability of appropriate printing capacity and paper, content management and related services, and technology support.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">PUBLISHING SEGMENT</font></b></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Dover, a subsidiary of the Company, is a publisher of books in over 30 specialty categories, including fine and commercial arts, children&#146;s books, crafts, music scores, graphic design, mathematics, physics and other areas of science, puzzles, games, social science, stationery items, and classics of literature for both juvenile and adult markets, including the Dover Thrift Editions</font><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#228;</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">.&#160; In 2005, Dover began developing proprietary packaged products under its Dover Fun Kits</font><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#228;</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> line.&#160; In 2008, Dover introduced a new premium series of hardcover reproductions, Dover Calla Editions</font><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#228;</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> and in 2012, launched a new adult coloring series, Creative Haven</font><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#228;</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> and an online image store, DoverPictura&#174;. In 2013, Dover introduced a new educational series branded Boost</font><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#228;</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Dover sells its products through most American bookstore chains, online retailers, independent booksellers, mass merchandisers, children&#146;s stores, craft stores and gift shops, as well as a diverse range of distributors around the world.&#160; Dover sells its e-books through all of the major e-book platforms. Dover has also sold its books directly to consumers for over 50 years through its specialty catalogs and over the Internet at www.doverpublications.com.&#160; Beginning in October&nbsp;2013 with the launch of its redesigned website, Dover is also selling ebooks directly from its website. Dover mails its proprietary catalogs to nearly 340,000 consumers and annually sends almost 135 million emails to electing customers.&#160; Dover also maintains www.DoverDirect.com, which is a business-to-business site for its retailers and distributors, and its image store at www.DoverPictura.com.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In the second quarter of fiscal 2009, due to a decline in sales and profits at Dover resulting from the continued downturn in the economic environment and in consumer spending, the Company recorded a non-cash, pre-tax impairment charge of $15.6 million, which represented 100% of Dover&#146;s goodwill.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">REA publishes more than 700 test preparation and study guide titles.&#160; Product lines include Problem Solvers&#174;, Essentials&#174;, Super Reviews&#174; and Test Preparation books, including its new Crash Course</font><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#228;</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;"> and All Access Series</font><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#228;</font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">.&#160; REA sells its products around the world through major bookseller chains, online retailers, college bookstores, and teachers&#146; supply stores, as well as directly to teachers and other consumers through catalogs and over the Internet at www.REA.com. REA sells its ebooks through all of the major e-book platforms.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In the third quarter of fiscal 2011, faced with the prospect of Borders Group,&nbsp;Inc.&#146;s liquidation, significant store closings and the permanent loss of what was an important customer, the Company concluded that the carrying value of REA&#146;s goodwill exceeded its estimated fair market value and a pre-tax impairment charge of $8.6 million was recorded, representing 100% of REA&#146;s goodwill as well as approximately $200,000 for prepublication costs related to underperforming titles.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Creative Homeowner is a publisher of books, home plans, and related products for the home and garden retail book market.&#160; Creative Homeowner&#146;s 95 titles include books on home decoration, design and improvement, as well as gardening and landscaping.&#160; Its products are sold primarily through home and garden centers and online retailers, as well as bookstores and direct to consumers over the Internet at www.creativehomeowner.com.&#160; From its line of home plan books, Creative Homeowner offers</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">3<a name="PB_3_161901_5796"></a></font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">over 10,000 home plans from which consumers can order blueprints directly over the Internet at www.ultimateplans.com.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In the third quarter of fiscal 2008, Creative Homeowner experienced a precipitous decline in sales and profits, due in large part to the downturn in the housing market and reduction in store traffic at home improvement centers and other large retail chain stores.&#160; As a result, the Company recorded a non-cash, pre-tax impairment charge of $23.6 million in fiscal 2008.&#160; In addition to other remedial measures, the Company decided to cease Creative Homeowner&#146;s book distribution operation that served a single customer, allowing it to concentrate on its principal publishing operations.&#160; This transition was completed in the second quarter of fiscal 2009.&#160; During the third quarter of fiscal 2010, the Company continued to integrate functions across this segment and consolidated Creative Homeowner&#146;s warehousing with the other publishing businesses in order to reduce costs.&#160; Despite these cost cutting measures, the prolonged weakness in the housing market led to a further decline in sales and operating results in the fourth quarter.&#160; As a result, the Company impaired the remaining goodwill and other intangible assets of Creative Homeowner, as well as $0.5 million of prepublication costs, resulting in a non-cash, pre-tax impairment charge of $4.7 million. In 2012, the Company reduced costs at Creative Homeowner by further integrating functions across the segment and narrowing the focus of its publishing program.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The U.S. publishing market is comprised of thousands of publishers, many of these publishers are much larger than Dover, REA, or Creative Homeowner, or are part of much larger organizations.&#160; In addition, newer sources of competition have emerged with large retailers launching or expanding publishing operations and with the continued adoption of e-books by consumers.&#160; In addition, new web-based publishing businesses are starting up.&#160; Dover distinguishes its products by offering an extremely wide variety of high quality books at modest prices.&#160; REA offers high quality study guides, test preparation books and software products in almost every academic area including many specialized areas such as teacher certification, adult education, and professional licensing.&#160; Creative Homeowner provides books on home improvement and landscaping that include high-quality photographs, illustrations and written content.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">MATERIALS AND SUPPLIES</font></b></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Courier purchases its principal raw materials, primarily paper, but also plate materials, ink, adhesives, cover stock, casebinding materials and cartons, from numerous suppliers, and is not dependent upon any one source for its requirements.&#160; Many of Courier&#146;s book manufacturing customers purchase their own paper and furnish it at no charge to Courier for book production.&#160; Dover, REA and Creative Homeowner purchase a significant portion of their books from Courier&#146;s book manufacturing operations. Paper prices have been relatively stable over the last eighteen months, although recent reductions in capacity may impact paper production.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">ENVIRONMENTAL REGULATIONS</font></b></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s operations are subject to federal, state and local environmental laws and regulations relating to, among other things: air emissions; waste generation, handling, management and disposal; wastewater treatment and discharge; and remediation of soil and groundwater contamination.&#160; The Company periodically makes capital expenditures so that its operations comply, in all material respects, with applicable environmental laws and regulations.&#160; No significant expenditures for this purpose were made in 2013 or are anticipated in 2014.&#160; In 2007, the Company adopted an &#147;Environmental, Health and Safety Policy&#148; which is available on the Company&#146;s website at www.courier.com. The Company does not believe that its compliance with applicable environmental laws and regulations will have a material impact on the Company&#146;s financial condition or liquidity.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">EMPLOYEES</font></b></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company employed 1,560 persons at September&nbsp;28, 2013 compared to 1,501 a year ago.&#160; The Company considers its relations with its employees to be satisfactory.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">OTHER</font></b></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Courier&#146;s educational sales, which represent over a third of its business, has seasonal demand which is highest in the second half of our fiscal year, with the peak season being in the Company&#146;s fourth quarter.&#160; The remainder of Courier&#146;s business is not significantly seasonal in nature.&#160; There is no portion of Courier&#146;s business subject to cancellation of government contracts or renegotiation of profits.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Courier does not hold any material patents, licenses, franchises or concessions upon which our operations are dependent, but does have trademarks, service marks, and Universal Resource Locators (URL&#146;s) on the Internet in connection with each of its business segments.&#160; Through its acquisitions of Highcrest Media and FastPencil, the Company owns certain customization and content management software utilized by its customers in the publishing and financial services industries.&#160; Substantially all of REA&#146;s and Creative Homeowner&#146;s publications and a majority of Dover&#146;s publications are protected by copyright, either in its own name, in the name of the author of the work, or in the name of a predecessor publisher from whom rights were acquired.&#160; Many of Dover&#146;s publications include works that are in the public domain.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company makes available free of charge (as soon as reasonably practicable after they are filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission) copies of its Annual Report on Form&nbsp;10-K, as well as all other reports required to be filed by Section&nbsp;13(a)&nbsp;or 15(d)&nbsp;of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, via the Internet at www.courier.com or upon written request to Peter M. <p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Item 1A.&#160; Risk Factors.</font></b><a name="Item1a_RiskFactors__161931"></a></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s consolidated results of operations, financial condition and cash flows can be adversely affected by various risks.&#160; Our business is influenced by many factors that are difficult to predict, involve uncertainties that may materially affect actual results and are often beyond our control.&#160; We discuss below the risks that we believe are material.&#160; You should carefully consider all of these factors.&#160; For other factors that may cause actual results to differ materially from those indicated in any forward-looking statement contained in this report, see <i>Forward-Looking Information</i> in <i>Management&#146;s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations</i>.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Industry competition and consolidation may increase pricing pressures and adversely impact our margins or result in a loss of customers.</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The book industry is extremely competitive.&#160; In the book manufacturing segment, consolidation over the past few years of both customers and competitors within the markets in which the Company competes has caused downward pricing pressures.&#160; In addition, excess capacity and competition from printing companies in lower cost countries may increase competitive pricing pressures.&#160; Furthermore, some of our competitors have greater sales, assets and financial resources than us, and those in foreign countries may derive significant advantages from local governmental regulation, including tax holidays and other subsidies.&#160; All or any of these competitive pressures could affect prices or customers&#146; demand for our products, impacting our profit margins and/or resulting in a loss of customers and market share.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">A reduction in orders or pricing from, or the loss of, any of our significant customers may adversely impact our operating results.</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We derived approximately 56% and 55% of our fiscal 2013 and 2012 revenues, respectively, from two major customers.&#160; We expect similar concentrations in fiscal 2014.&#160; We do business with these customers on a purchase order basis and they are not bound to purchase at particular volume levels.&#160; As a result, either of these customers could determine to reduce their order volume or pricing with us, especially if our pricing is not deemed competitive.&#160; A significant reduction in order volumes or pricing from, or the loss of, either of these customers could have a material adverse effect on our results of operations and financial condition.&#160; In addition, our publishing segment is dependent on Amazon as a</font></p>

Tightness in credit markets may also affect our ability to consummate such acquisitions.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In our publishing segment, sales to retailers and distributors are highly concentrated on a small group, which previously included Borders Group,&nbsp;Inc. (&#147;Borders&#148;). Any bankruptcy, liquidation, insolvency or other failure of a major retailer or distributor could also have a material impact on the Company.&#160; For example, during fiscal 2011, we recorded a bad debt expense of $700,000 related to the Borders&#146; bankruptcy and liquidation. As a result of the impact of the Borders situation, in the third quarter of fiscal 2011, the Company recorded a pre-tax impairment charge of $8.6 million, representing 100% of REA&#146;s goodwill as well as approximately $200,000 for prepublication costs related to underperforming titles.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Electronic delivery of content may adversely affect our business.</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Electronic delivery of content offers an alternative to the traditional delivery through print.&#160; Widespread consumer acceptance of electronic delivery of books is uncertain, as is the extent to which consumers are willing to replace print materials with online hosted media content.&#160; If our customers&#146; acceptance of electronic delivery of books and online hosted media content continues to grow, demand for and/or pricing of our printed products may be adversely affected. Non-profit organizations have worked to encourage development of educational content that can be &#147;open sourced&#148; for educational purposes.&#160; If these initiatives increase the availability and utilization of free or inexpensive materials online, it may adversely impact sales, reduce demand or change customer expectations regarding pricing and delivery.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">We could face significant liability as a result of our participation in multi-employer pension plans.</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We participate in two multi-employer defined benefit pension plans for certain union employees. Multi-employer pension plans cover employees of and receive contributions from two or more unrelated employers under one or more union contracts. Our risks of participating in these types of plans include the fact that (i)&nbsp;plan contributions by each employer, including us, may be used to provide benefits to employees of other participating employers, (ii)&nbsp;if another participating employer withdraws from either plan, the unfunded obligations of the plan may be borne by the remaining participating employers, including us, and (iii)&nbsp;if we withdraw from participating in either plan, we may be required to pay the plan an amount based on our allocable share of the underfunded status of the plan.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We make periodic contributions to two multi-employer plans pursuant to our union contracts, each of which was renewed in fiscal year 2013, to allow the plans to meet the pension benefit obligations to plan participants.&nbsp;We currently expect that we will be required to contribute approximately $352,000 to these two plans in fiscal 2014, but these contributions could significantly increase due to other employers&#146; withdrawals or changes in the funded status of the plans. Further, if we continue to participate in such pension plans, our contributions may increase depending on the outcome of future union negotiations and applicable law, changes in the funding status of the plans, and any reduction in participation or withdrawal by other employers from the plans.&nbsp;Our continued participation in these plans could have a material adverse impact on our results of operations, cash flows or financial condition. In the event that we withdraw from participation in one or both of these plans, we could be required to make a withdrawal liability payment or series of payments to the plan, which would be reflected as an expense in our consolidated statements of operations and a liability on our consolidated balance sheet. Our withdrawal liability for any multiemployer plan would depend on the funded status of the plan and the level of our prior plan contributions.&nbsp; Both plans are estimated to be underfunded as of September&nbsp;28, 2013 and have a Pension Protection Act zone status of critical (&#147;red&#148;); such status identifies plans that are less than 65% funded. In addition, our contributions to the Bindery Industry Employers GCC/IBT Pension Plan represented approximately 70% of total contributions in each of the last three years.&#160; This plan currently includes only two other contributing employers.&nbsp; A withdrawal by one or more of these employers could materially increase the amount of our required contributions to this plan.&#160; A future withdrawal by us from either of the two multi-employer pension plans could result in a withdrawal</font></p>

<div style="font-family:Times New Roman;">
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">liability for us, the amount of which could be material to our results of operations, cash flows and financial condition.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">A failure to successfully adapt to changing book sales channels may have an adverse impact on our business.</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Over the last several years, the &#147;bricks&nbsp;&amp; mortar&#148; bookstore channel has experienced a significant contraction, including the bankruptcy of Borders Group,&nbsp;Inc. and Nebraska Book Co., the closure of many independent bookstores, and the reduction in inventory and shelf space for books in other national chains.&#160; In addition to expanding our online and direct to consumer sales, we have responded by offering over 4,000 of our titles as ebooks, as well as seeking alternative channels for our products, such as mass merchandising chains.&#160; However, there is no guarantee that we will be able to address the challenges in these channels, including creating price competitive products that will successfully penetrate these markets and accurately predicting the volume of returns.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Declines in general economic conditions may adversely impact our business.</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Economic conditions have the potential to impact our financial results significantly.&#160; Within the book manufacturing and publishing segments, we may be adversely affected by the current worldwide economic downturn, including as a result of changes in government, business and consumer spending.&#160; Examples of how our financial results may be impacted include:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Fluctuations in federal or state government spending on education, including a reduction in tax revenues due to the current economic environment, could lead to a corresponding decrease in the demand for educational materials, which are produced in our book manufacturing segment and comprise a portion of our publishing products.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Consumer demand for books can be impacted by reductions in disposable income when costs such as electricity and gasoline reduce discretionary spending.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Tightness in credit markets may result in customers delaying orders to reduce inventory levels and may impact their ability to pay their debts as they become due and may disrupt supplies from vendors, and may result in customers becoming insolvent.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Changes in the housing market may impact the sale of Creative Homeowner&#146;s products.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Reduced fundraising by religious customers may decrease their order levels.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">A slowdown in book purchases may result in retailers returning an unusually large number of books to publishers to reduce their inventories.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">A failure to keep pace with rapid industrial and technological change may have an adverse impact on our business.</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The printing industry is in a period of rapid technological evolution.&#160; Our future financial performance will depend, in part, upon the ability to anticipate and adapt to rapid industrial and technological changes occurring in the industry and upon the ability to offer, on a timely basis, services that meet evolving industry standards.&#160; If we are unable to adapt to such technological changes, we may lose customers and may not be able to maintain our competitive position. In addition, we may encounter difficulties in the implementation and start-up of new equipment and technology.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We are unable to predict which of the many possible future product and service offerings will be important to establish and maintain a competitive position or what expenditures will be required to develop and provide these products and services.&#160; We cannot assure investors that one or more of these factors will not vary unpredictably, which could have a material adverse effect on us. In addition, we cannot assure investors, even if these factors turn out as we anticipate, that we will be able to implement our strategy or that the strategy will be successful in this rapidly evolving market.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Our operating results are unpredictable and fluctuate significantly, which may adversely affect our stock price.</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our quarterly and annual operating results have fluctuated in the past and are likely to fluctuate in the future due to a variety of factors, some of which are outside of our control. Factors that may affect our future operating results include:</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">the timing and size of the orders for our books;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">the availability of markets for sales or distribution by our major customers;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">the lengthy and unpredictable sales cycles associated with sales of textbooks to the elementary and high school market;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">the migration of educators and students towards electronic delivery of content;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">our customers&#146; willingness and success in shifting orders from the peak textbook season to the off-peak season to even out our manufacturing load over the year;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">fluctuations in the currency market may make manufacturing in the United States more or less attractive and make equipment more or less expensive for us to purchase;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">issues that might arise from the integration of acquired businesses, including their inability to achieve expected results; and</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">tightness in credit markets affecting the availability of capital for ourselves, our vendors, and/or our customers.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt .5in;text-indent:-.25in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As a result of these and other factors, period-to-period comparisons of our operating results are not necessarily meaningful or indicative of future performance. In addition, the factors noted above may make it difficult for us to forecast and provide in a timely manner public guidance (including updates to prior guidance) related to our projected financial performance. Furthermore, it is possible that in future quarters our operating results could fall below the expectations of securities analysts or investors. If this occurs, the trading price of our common stock could decline.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Our financial results could be negatively impacted by impairments of goodwill or other intangible assets, or other long-lived assets.</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We perform an annual assessment for impairment of goodwill and other intangible assets, as well as other long-lived assets, at the end of our fiscal year or whenever events or changes in circumstances occur that would more likely than not reduce the fair value of a reporting unit below its carrying value, including a downturn in the market value of the Company&#146;s stock.&#160; A downward revision in the fair value of one of our acquired businesses could result in impairments of goodwill and non-cash charges.&#160; Any impairment charge could have a significant negative effect on our reported results of operations.&#160; For example, at the end of the third quarter of fiscal 2011, the Company determined that the fair value of REA was below its carrying value and a pre-tax impairment charge of $8.6 million was recorded, which represented 100% of REA&#146;s goodwill as well as approximately $200,000 for prepublication costs related to underperforming titles and long-lived assets.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Fluctuations in the cost and availability of paper and other raw materials may cause disruption and impact margins.</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Purchases of paper and other raw materials represent a large portion of our costs. &#160;In our book manufacturing segment, paper is normally supplied by our customers at their expense or price increases are passed through to our customers.&#160; In our publishing segment, cost increases have generally been passed on to customers through higher prices or we have substituted a less expensive grade of paper.&#160; However, if we are unable to continue to pass on these increases or substitute a less expensive grade of paper, our margins and profits could be adversely affected.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Availability of paper is important to both our book manufacturing and publishing segments.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Although we generally have not experienced difficulty in obtaining adequate supplies of paper, recent reductions in capacity may impact paper production and unexpected changes in the paper markets could result in a shortage of supply.&#160; If this were to occur in the future, it could cause disruption to the business or increase paper costs, adversely impacting either or both net sales or profits.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Fluctuations in the costs and availability of paper and other raw materials could adversely affect operating costs or customer demand and thereby negatively impact our operating results, financial condition or cash flows.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In addition, fluctuations in the markets for paper and other raw materials may adversely affect the market for our waste byproducts, including recycled paper, and used plates, and therefore adversely affect our income from such sales.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Energy costs and availability may negatively impact our financial results.</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Energy costs are incurred directly to run production equipment and facilities and indirectly through expenses such as freight and raw materials such as ink.&#160; In a competitive market environment, increases to these direct and indirect energy related costs might not be able to be passed through to customers through price increases or mitigated through other means.&#160; In such instances, increased energy costs could adversely impact operating costs or customer demand.&#160; In addition, interruption in the availability of energy could disrupt operations, adversely impacting operating results.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Inadequate intellectual property protection for our publications could negatively impact our financial results.</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Certain of our publications are protected by copyright, primarily held in the Company&#146;s name.&#160; Such copyrights protect our exclusive right to publish the work in the United States and in many other countries for specified periods.&#160; Our ability to continue to achieve anticipated results depends in part on our ability to defend our intellectual property against infringement.&#160; Our operating results may be adversely affected by inadequate legal and technological protections for intellectual property and proprietary rights in some jurisdictions and markets.&#160; In addition, some of our publications are of works in the public domain, for which there is nearly no intellectual property protection.&#160; Our operating results may be adversely affected by the increased availability of such works elsewhere, including on the Internet, either for free or for a lower price.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">A failure to maintain or improve our operating efficiencies could adversely impact our profitability.</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Because the markets in which we operate are highly competitive, we must continue to improve our operating efficiency in order to maintain or improve our profitability.&#160; Although we have been able to expand our capacity, improve our productivity and reduce costs in the past, there is no assurance that we will be able to do so in the future.&#160; In addition, reducing operating costs in the future may require significant initial costs to reduce headcount, close or consolidate operations, or upgrade equipment and technology.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Our facilities are subject to stringent environmental laws and regulations, which may subject us to liability or increase our costs.</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We use various materials in our operations that contain substances considered hazardous or toxic under environmental laws.&#160; In addition, our operations are subject to federal, state, and local environmental laws relating to, among other things, air emissions, waste generation, handling, management and disposal, waste water treatment and discharge and remediation of soil and groundwater contamination.&#160; Permits are required for the operation of certain of our businesses and these permits are subject to renewal, modification and in some circumstances, revocation.&#160; Under certain environmental laws, including the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation and Liability Act, as amended (&#147;CERCLA,&#148; commonly referred to as &#147;Superfund&#148;), and similar state laws and regulations, we may be liable for costs and damages relating to soil and groundwater contamination at off-site disposal</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;"><a href="#TableOfContents" title="Click to go to Table of Contents">Table of Contents</a></font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">locations or at our facilities.&#160; Future changes to environmental laws and regulations may give rise to additional costs or liabilities that could have a material adverse impact on our financial position and results of operations.</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">A failure to hire and train key executives and other qualified employees could adversely affect our business.</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our success depends, in part, on our ability to continue to retain our executive officers and key management personnel.&#160; Our business strategy also depends on our ability to attract, develop, motivate and retain employees who have relevant experience in the printing and publishing industries.&#160; There can be no assurance that we can continue to attract and retain the necessary talented employees, including executive officers and other key members of management and, if we fail to do so, it could adversely affect our business.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">A lack of skilled employees to manufacture our products may adversely affect our business.</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">If we experience problems hiring and retaining skilled employees, our business may be negatively affected.&#160; The timely manufacture and delivery of our products requires an adequate supply of skilled employees, and the operating costs of our manufacturing facilities can be adversely affected by high turnover in skilled positions.&#160; Accordingly, our ability to increase sales, productivity and net earnings could be impacted by our ability to employ the skilled employees necessary to meet our requirements.&#160; Although our book manufacturing locations are geographically dispersed, individual locations may encounter strong competition with other manufacturers for skilled employees.&#160; There can be no assurance that we will be able to maintain an adequate skilled labor force necessary to efficiently operate our facilities.&#160; In addition, unions represent certain groups of employees at one of our locations, and periodically, contracts with those unions come up for renewal.&#160; The outcome of those negotiations could have an adverse effect on our operations at that location.&#160; Also, changes in federal and/or state laws may facilitate the organization of unions at locations that do not currently have unions, which could have an adverse effect on our operations.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">We are subject to various laws and regulations that may require significant expenditures.</font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We are subject to federal, state and local laws and regulations affecting our business, including those promulgated under the Consumer Product Safety Act, the rules&nbsp;and regulations of the Consumer Products Safety Commission as well as laws and regulations relating to personal information.&#160; We may be required to make significant expenditures to comply with such governmental laws and regulations and any amendments thereto. Complying with existing or future laws or regulations may materially limit our business and increase our costs.&#160; Failure to comply with such laws may expose us to potential liability and have a material adverse effect on our results of operations.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Item 1B.&#160; Unresolved Staff Comments.</font></b><a name="Item1b_UnresolvedStaffComments__162255"></a></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">None.</font></p>

A portion of the facility was used for warehousing at September&nbsp;28, 2013. A 40,000 square foot section was sublet effective March&nbsp;2013 through October&nbsp;2015, which is the end of the lease term.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt 33.0pt;text-indent:-33.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">EQUIPMENT</font></b></p>
<p align="center" style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s products are manufactured on equipment that in most cases is owned by the Company, although it leases certain computers and other equipment, which are subject to more rapid obsolescence.&#160; Capital expenditures amounted to approximately $22.2 million in 2013, $9.9 million in 2012, and $15.7 million in 2011. Capital expenditures for fiscal 2014 are expected to be between $14 and $16 million, approximately $10 million of which relates to expansion of the Company&#146;s digital print capabilities. Courier considers its equipment to be in good operating condition and adequate for its present needs.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On November&nbsp;21, 2013, the Company announced the approval by its Board of Directors for the repurchase of up to $10 million of the Company&#146;s outstanding common stock from time to time on the open market or in privately negotiated transactions, including pursuant to a Rule&nbsp;10b5-1 nondiscretionary trading plan. This stock repurchase authorization is effective for a period of twelve months.&#160; During fiscal 2013, the Company repurchased 123,261 shares of common stock for approximately $1.6 million under a similar program which expired November&nbsp;20, 2013. In April&nbsp;2012, the Company&#146;s Board of Directors had approved a similar program for the repurchase of up to $10 million of the Company&#146;s outstanding common stock. During the second half of fiscal 2012, the Company repurchased 823,970 shares of common stock for approximately $10 million under that program.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Item 7A.&#160; Quantitative and Qualitative Disclosures About Market Risk.</font></b><a name="Item7a_QuantitativeAndQualitative_161626"></a></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;text-indent:.5in;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company does not hold any derivative financial instruments, derivative commodity instruments or other financial instruments.&#160; At September&nbsp;28, 2013, the Company had a forward exchange contract to sell approximately 11 million South African Rands (ZAR) as a hedge against the future sales proceeds of approximately $1.2 million, which was designated as a cash flow hedge. The fair value of the foreign exchange forward contract was valued using market exchange rates.&#160; The Company engages neither in speculative nor derivative trading activities. The Company is exposed to market risk for changes in interest rates on invested funds as well as borrowed funds.&#160; The Company&#146;s revolving bank credit facility bears interest at a floating rate, with further information contained in Note D of Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements of this Annual Report on Form&nbsp;10-K.&#160; The Company believes it is remote that this could have a material impact on results of operations.</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Item 8.&#160; Financial Statements and Supplementary Data.<a name="Item8_FinancialStatementsAndSuppl_161629"></a></font></b></p>
<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0in 0in .0001pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Item 9.&#160; Changes in and Disagreements With Accountants on Accounting and Financial Disclosure.</font></b><a name="Item9_ChangesInAndDisagreementsWi_161630"></a></p>
